mantis_folded_arms_and_insect_grip.title: Why Does a Mantis Hold Its Arms Up?
mantis_folded_arms_and_insect_grip.script: Why does this mantis hold its front legs up, almost like it is waving? Those folded legs have spines that help the insect grip things close to its body. When a smaller insect is caught, the mantis uses those arms to keep its meal from escaping. Other close recordings show how carefully the animal positions those same front legs. A raised posture can also appear when a mantis responds to something around it. Whether it is handling prey or holding still, those front legs are its most remarkable tools.
mantis_folded_arms_and_insect_grip.caption: WHY DOES A MANTIS HOLD ITS ARMS UP? #WildVox #Animals #Nature #Wildlife

kingfisher_digging_and_fishing_bill.title: What Does a Kingfisher Do Before It Catches Fish?
kingfisher_digging_and_fishing_bill.script: This tiny kingfisher is working at a riverbank instead of diving after a fish. A bird that feeds near water still needs a sheltered place to raise its young. In this recording, it visits a small opening in the bank where a nest tunnel is being made. Other kingfishers can be seen resting or moving along the edges of different waterways. Later, the pointed bill has another job when a kingfisher handles a caught fish. The same small bird can work at its nest and bring home food with one remarkable bill.
kingfisher_digging_and_fishing_bill.caption: A KINGFISHER HAS MORE THAN ONE JOB FOR ITS BILL. #WildVox #Birds #Wildlife #Nature

bald_eagle_small_bites_for_eaglets.title: Why Do Bald Eagle Parents Feed Such Small Bites?
bald_eagle_small_bites_for_eaglets.script: An adult bald eagle has a powerful beak, but its chicks still need very small meals. Young eaglets cannot catch their own fish, so adults must bring food to the nest. Here another parent bends toward the nest, offering food to growing young birds. Across other places, adult bald eagles keep searching, flying, and watching their surroundings. Even these powerful birds can be chased by smaller birds near a territory. Long before a young eagle can hunt, its survival depends on the adults that feed it.
bald_eagle_small_bites_for_eaglets.caption: WHY EAGLETS NEED SMALL BITES. #WildVox #Eagles #AnimalFacts #Wildlife

beaver_zoo_land_and_water_movement.title: Why Does a Beaver Move So Differently Near Water?
beaver_zoo_land_and_water_movement.script: This North American beaver was filmed at a zoo, where its heavy body is easy to see. On the ground, the animal carries a broad body and stays close to the enclosure. When it enters water, that same body is supported as it moves and paddles. A beaver also has dense fur that helps protect it in its watery habitat. Watch how different the animal can look when it is moving through water. These zoo recordings give a close look at a rodent adapted for life beside water.
beaver_zoo_land_and_water_movement.caption: A BEAVER'S BODY IS BUILT FOR WATER. Filmed in a zoo. #WildVox #Beavers #AnimalFacts #Nature

goats_grazing_grooming_and_nursing.title: What Do Goats Do When They Stop Grazing?
goats_grazing_grooming_and_nursing.script: These goats are spread across a grassy hillside, but feeding is not their only activity. A different herd moves over rocky ground, looking for the next place to stop. Some goats eat hay, while others choose grass in another open field. Between meals, goats may pause to groom, yawn, or simply rest for a while. Newborn kids have another priority: getting milk from their mother before they can graze. From small kids to roaming adults, a goat herd is always doing more than eating.
goats_grazing_grooming_and_nursing.caption: WHAT GOATS DO BETWEEN MEALS. #WildVox #Goats #FarmAnimals #AnimalFacts
